newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium crumbles on LME, touches 2-1/2 low.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium crumbles on LME, touches 2-1/2 low.

text.p: Aluminium spun lower during Wednesday LME trading, as the market came under persistent speculative selling pressure which knocked away potential support levels, traders said.
Elsewhere in a distinctly off-colour metals complex there were losses seen in copper as Tuesday's upside enthusiasm evaporated, and a setback in nickel values.
"The market definitely did not have a lot going for it today. Copper looks as if it is just ranging, but aluminium could well go much lower," one trader said.

Aluminium was knocked off its stride by commission house sales and liquidation, which resulted in previous lows and the important $1,330 level giving way. The tide was halted just below $1,320, with prices bottoming at $1,316, but the market seems destined to head under $1,300 soon.
Last kerb trade today was at $1,323 a tonne, down $23.50 from Tuesday's kerb close.

Copper turned lower once the early attempt to run the market above $1,950 and re-challenge $1,970 faltered. The spreads were less tight also, as yesterday's generalised covering against short dates has run its course.
Last business was at $1,928, down $21 from yesterday, with a well-defined $1,900/10 to $1,950/70 range available for the market to fluctuate in short-term.

Nickel prices stabilised during slow afternoon trading, after liquidation at midsession sent the market into a tail-spin from near the $7,200 level. Last trade was at $7,130 a tonne, down $120 from yesterday.
Traders said news that Inco will lose around 2,000 tonnes of production in Indonesia did not exite the market, as the furnace problems occured last month.
Lead drifted lower in lacklustre conditions, but did not decline too far with the cash/threes spread holding near parity. Last three months business was at $766, down $6 from Tuesday.
Zinc was generally content to trade in a narrow range around overnight levels in the mid-$1,030s. The market ended the session at $1,034, down just $1 from yesterday.
Tin reversed direction after a steadier start, but trading was slow and the downward drift was gentle. Prices closed down just $5 at $6,055.
The alloy market was depressed by the fresh losses in primary, with business taking place under the $1,200 level. The kerb concluded at $1,195, down $20.
